subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: In which year was the first General Election of independent India successfully completed?
questions.explanation: The first General Election in India was held from October 1951 to February 1952, and is generally referred to as the 1952 election.

questions.question: Who served as the first Chief Election Commissioner of independent India?
questions.explanation: Sukumar Sen, an Indian Civil Service officer, was appointed as India's first Chief Election Commissioner in March 1950.

questions.question: Which political party emerged as the second-largest party in terms of Lok Sabha seats in the first General Election of 1952?
questions.explanation: The Communist Party of India (CPI) won 16 seats in the 1952 Lok Sabha election, emerging as the largest opposition group.

questions.question: Who was the Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India who played the historic role in integrating the princely states into the Indian Union?
questions.explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, often called the 'Iron Man of India', diplomatically persuaded and integrated over 500 princely states into the Indian Union.

questions.question: What was the official legal document signed by the rulers of princely states consenting to join the Union of India called?
questions.explanation: Rulers of princely states signed the 'Instrument of Accession', agreeing to surrender defense, foreign affairs, and communications to the Indian Union.

questions.question: Which veteran Gandhian leader undertook an indefinite hunger strike leading to his death in 1952, sparking the demand for the linguistic state of Andhra?
questions.explanation: Potti Sreeramulu died after a 56-day fast on 15 December 1952, which forced the central government to announce the creation of the separate state of Andhra in December 1952.

questions.question: In which year did the central government appoint the States Reorganisation Commission headed by Justice Fazal Ali?
questions.explanation: The States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) was appointed in December 1953 with Justice Fazal Ali, K.M. Panikkar, and Hriday Nath Kunzru as members.

questions.question: In which year was the Planning Commission of India established by a resolution of the Government of India?
questions.explanation: The Planning Commission was set up in March 1950 by an executive resolution of the Cabinet as an extra-constitutional advisory body with the Prime Minister as Chairman.

questions.question: The First Five Year Plan (1951-1956) in India placed its primary emphasis on which sector?
questions.explanation: The First Five Year Plan primarily focused on the agrarian sector, including substantial investments in dams, irrigation, and agriculture to overcome post-partition food shortages.

questions.question: Who was the renowned statistician and founder of the Indian Statistical Institute who formulated the strategy for the Second Five Year Plan?
questions.explanation: Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis drafted the Second Five Year Plan, which focused on rapid industrialisation and the heavy state-led capital goods sector.

questions.question: Verghese Kurien is famously celebrated as the 'Milkman of India' for leading which nationwide rural development programme?
questions.explanation: Verghese Kurien spearheaded the dairy cooperative movement centered in Anand, Gujarat, initiating 'Operation Flood' in 1970.

questions.question: Which five principles of peaceful coexistence were jointly signed by Indian Prime Minister Nehru and Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai in April 1954?
questions.explanation: The Panchsheel (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence) was signed between Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Premier Zhou Enlai on 29 April 1954.

questions.question: Where was the historic Afro-Asian Conference held in 1955 that laid the foundational groundwork for the Non-Aligned Movement?
questions.explanation: The Afro-Asian Conference held in Bandung, Indonesia, in 1955 brought together 29 newly independent nations and led directly to the birth of the Non-Aligned Movement.

questions.question: Where was the first official summit conference of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) held in September 1961?
questions.explanation: The first NAM Summit was convened in Belgrade in September 1961, attended by 25 member states under the leadership of Nehru, Tito, Nasser, Sukarno, and Nkrumah.

questions.question: In which month and year did India conduct its first peaceful nuclear explosion test at Pokhran, Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: India carried out its first underground nuclear explosion at Pokhran under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on 18 May 1974, code-named 'Smiling Buddha'.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Who succeeded Jawaharlal Nehru as the Prime Minister of India following Nehru's demise in May 1964?
questions.explanation: Lal Bahadur Shastri was unanimously chosen by the Congress Party as Prime Minister in June 1964 following Jawaharlal Nehru's death.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which famous rallying slogan was coined by Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri during the Indo-Pak War of 1965?
questions.explanation: Lal Bahadur Shastri gave the inspiring slogan 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' ('Hail the Soldier, Hail the Farmer') to motivate soldiers and agricultural producers during the 1965 war and food crisis.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which political slogan formed the centerpiece of Indira Gandhi's election campaign in the 1971 Lok Sabha elections?
questions.explanation: In 1971, while the Grand Alliance opposition coalition campaigned on 'Indira Hatao', Indira Gandhi counter-attacked with the positive socio-economic slogan 'Garibi Hatao'.

questions.question: Which socialist leader led the Bihar movement in 1974 and gave the call for 'Total Revolution' (Sampoorna Kranti)?
questions.explanation: Jayaprakash Narayan (JP) accepted the leadership of the student agitation in Bihar in 1974 and demanded 'Total Revolution' in social, economic, and political spheres.

questions.question: On which exact date was the National Emergency declared by President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed on the advice of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi?
questions.explanation: The National Emergency was proclaimed on the night of 25 June 1975 under Article 352 of the Constitution on the grounds of internal disturbance.

questions.question: Which commission of inquiry was appointed in May 1977 by the Janata Party government to investigate the excesses committed during the Emergency?
questions.explanation: The Janata Party government appointed the Shah Commission, headed by retired Chief Justice of India J.C. Shah, to investigate abuses of authority and malpractices during the Emergency.

questions.question: Who became the first non-Congress Prime Minister of India following the historic general elections of March 1977?
questions.explanation: Morarji Desai took oath as India's first non-Congress Prime Minister in March 1977 leading the Janata Party government.

questions.question: The Mandal Commission was established in 1978 to identify and recommend reservations for which section of Indian society?
questions.explanation: The Second Backward Classes Commission, popularly known as the Mandal Commission (chaired by B.P. Mandal), was appointed to investigate conditions of the Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (OBCs).

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: The fall of which iconic structure in November 1989 symbolized the beginning of the collapse of the communist bloc in Eastern Europe?
questions.explanation: The demolition of the Berlin Wall by ordinary citizens on 9 November 1989 marked the dramatic collapse of the division between Eastern and Western Europe.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Who was the last General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union who introduced the reform policies of Perestroika and Glasnost?
questions.explanation: Mikhail Gorbachev became General Secretary in 1985 and initiated Perestroika (restructuring) and Glasnost (openness) to revitalize the Soviet system.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: What painful model of economic transition from communism to capitalism was prescribed for post-Soviet states by the World Bank and IMF?
questions.explanation: The sudden, wholesale transition from an authoritarian socialist system to a free-market capitalist system in post-Soviet countries was known as 'Shock Therapy'.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which historic treaty signed in February 1992 formally established the European Union (EU)?
questions.explanation: The Treaty on European Union was signed in Maastricht, Netherlands, on 7 February 1992, creating the European Union and paving the way for the common currency, the Euro.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) was established in August 1967 through the signing of which declaration?
questions.explanation: ASEAN was founded on 8 August 1967 when foreign ministers of Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand signed the Bangkok Declaration.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Who was the Chinese premier who introduced the 'Four Modernisations' in agriculture, industry, defense, and science & technology in 1973?
questions.explanation: Premier Zhou Enlai proposed the 'Four Modernisations' in 1973, which were later vigorously implemented under Deng Xiaoping's economic leadership.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: In which city was the first summit of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) held in December 1985?
questions.explanation: The first SAARC Summit took place in Dhaka, Bangladesh, on 7-8 December 1985, bringing together seven South Asian heads of state and government.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: The militant organisation Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) was involved in an armed ethnic conflict in which South Asian island country?
questions.explanation: The LTTE waged an armed separatist campaign from 1983 to 2009 for an independent Tamil homeland (Tamil Eelam) in the north and east of Sri Lanka.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: On which date is United Nations (UN) Day celebrated globally every year to commemorate the entry into force of the UN Charter?
questions.explanation: United Nations Day is observed on 24 October each year, marking the day in 1945 when the UN Charter came into force with ratifications by the majority of signatories.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: How many permanent members hold the veto power in the United Nations Security Council (UNSC)?
questions.explanation: The UNSC has 5 permanent members (United States, Russia, United Kingdom, France, and China) who possess veto power under the UN Charter.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: The landmark United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED), popular as the 'Earth Summit', was held in 1992 in which city?
questions.explanation: The Earth Summit took place in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in June 1992, producing Agenda 21, the Rio Declaration, and conventions on climate change and biodiversity.

questions.question: What is the global platform of environmentalists, labor unions, human rights activists, and feminists that organizes meetings against neo-liberal globalisation?
options: D) Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD)
questions.explanation: The World Social Forum (WSF) was formed as an alternative global coalition opposing neo-liberal economic globalisation, holding its first gathering in Porto Alegre, Brazil, in 2001.

questions.question: Which political thinker formulated the strategic concept of 'Non-Congressism' to unite opposition parties against the Congress before the 1967 elections?
questions.explanation: Socialist leader Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia gave the theoretical rationale of 'Non-Congressism', arguing that Congress rule was undemocratic and an alliance of all non-Congress parties was essential to restore power to the people.

questions.question: In which state did the Communist Party of India form the world's first democratically elected communist state government in 1957?
questions.explanation: In March 1957, the CPI won 60 out of 126 seats in Kerala and formed the government under Chief Minister E.M.S. Namboodiripad, becoming the first democratically elected communist ministry.

questions.question: The ruler of which princely state signed the Instrument of Accession on the condition of maintaining the internal autonomy under the Maharaja Bodhachandra Singh?
questions.explanation: Maharaja Bodhachandra Singh of Manipur signed the Instrument of Accession after receiving assurances that the internal autonomy of Manipur would be preserved.

questions.question: Which Gandhian economist proposed an alternative blueprint for planning emphasizing rural industrialization and village economy entitled 'Economy of Permanence'?
questions.explanation: J.C. Kumarappa (originally J.C. Cornelius), a Gandhian economist, advocated a human-centric rural economic plan centered on self-reliant village industries in his work 'Economy of Permanence'.

questions.question: The 1966 Tashkent Agreement to restore peaceful ties between India and Pakistan was brokered by which foreign power?
questions.explanation: Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin mediated the Tashkent Agreement between Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri and Pakistani President Ayub Khan in January 1966.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the 1969 presidential election, which independent candidate did Indira Gandhi openly support against the official Congress nominee N. Sanjiva Reddy?
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi called for a 'conscience vote' and backed Vice-President V.V. Giri as an independent candidate, who successfully defeated the official Congress Syndicate nominee Neelam Sanjiva Reddy.

questions.question: Which historic verdict of the Allahabad High Court on 12 June 1975 declared Indira Gandhi's 1971 election to the Lok Sabha invalid on an election petition filed by Raj Narain?
options: A) Judgment delivered by Justice A.N. Ray
B) Judgment delivered by Justice Jagmohan Lal Sinha
C) Judgment delivered by Justice H.R. Khanna
D) Judgment delivered by Justice Y.V. Chandrachud
questions.explanation: Justice Jagmohan Lal Sinha of the Allahabad High Court ruled on 12 June 1975 that Indira Gandhi had used government officials for her election campaign, thus setting aside her election from Rae Bareli.

questions.question: Under whose leadership did the All Assam Students Union (AASU) launch the six-year-long anti-foreigner agitation beginning in 1979?
options: C) Prafulla Kumar Mahanta and Bhrigu Kumar Phukan
questions.explanation: AASU leaders Prafulla Kumar Mahanta and Bhrigu Kumar Phukan led the mass agitation against illegal migrants from 1979, which culminated in the signing of the Assam Accord in August 1985.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: What is the collective term for the three specialized pillars of the ASEAN Community established in 2003?
options: A) ASEAN Defense Council, ASEAN Trade Pact, and ASEAN Diplomatic Forum
B) ASEAN Monetary Union, ASEAN Military Command, and ASEAN Labour Union
C) ASEAN Maritime League, ASEAN Tariff Union, and ASEAN Justice Forum
D) ASEAN Security Community, ASEAN Economic Community, and ASEAN Socio-Cultural Community
questions.explanation: In 2003, ASEAN leaders established the ASEAN Community comprising three distinct pillars: the ASEAN Security Community, the ASEAN Economic Community, and the ASEAN Socio-Cultural Community.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: In which year did the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement come into active effect across SAARC nations?
questions.explanation: SAFTA was signed by SAARC leaders in January 2004 during the 12th SAARC Summit in Islamabad and came into official effect on 1 January 2006.

questions.question: Which multilateral arms control treaty entered into force in 1970 to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons and weapons technology?
questions.explanation: The Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT) opened for signature in 1968 and entered into force in 1970, which India refused to sign citing its discriminatory nature.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: The principle of 'Common But Differentiated Responsibilities' (CBDR) was formally enunciated in which international document?
options: C) Rio Declaration at the 1992 Earth Summit
questions.explanation: Principle 7 of the Rio Declaration adopted at the 1992 Earth Summit explicitly recognized that states have common responsibilities but differing capacities and historical roles in global environmental degradation.

questions.question: In the landmark Kesavananda Bharati judgment of April 1973, which sole dissenting senior judge was later superseded when Indira Gandhi appointed A.N. Ray as the Chief Justice of India, setting aside established judicial seniority convention?
options: A) Justice H.R. Khanna, Justice Y.V. Chandrachud, and Justice P.N. Bhagwati were superseded
B) Justice M.H. Beg, Justice P.B. Gajendragadkar, and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer were superseded
C) Justice Subba Rao, Justice K. Subba Rao, and Justice S.M. Sikri were superseded
D) Justice J.M. Shelat, Justice K.S. Hegde, and Justice A.N. Grover were superseded
questions.explanation: Following Chief Justice S.M. Sikri's retirement in April 1973, the government appointed Justice A.N. Ray as CJI, superseding three senior judges—Justices J.M. Shelat, K.S. Hegde, and A.N. Grover—who had ruled against the government in the basic structure verdict.

questions.question: Which political resolution passed by the Shiromani Akali Dal at Anandpur Sahib in October 1973 demanded a restructuring of Centre-State relations and greater autonomy for Punjab?
questions.explanation: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution passed in 1973 asserted regional autonomy, demanding that the Centre restrict its jurisdiction to defense, foreign affairs, communications, and currency, while all residual powers vest with the states.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: In December 1991, the leaders of which three key Soviet republics met in Belovezha Forest and signed the Belavezha Accords, formally declaring the dissolution of the Soviet Union and establishing the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)?
questions.explanation: On 8 December 1991, President Boris Yeltsin of Russia, President Leonid Kravchuk of Ukraine, and Chairman Stanislav Shushkevich of Belarus signed the Belavezha Accords, ending the USSR and establishing the CIS.
